Wetherby School: Two Pathways, One Exceptional Education in London
For more than 75 years, Wetherby has been synonymous with exceptional independent education in London, combining academic ambition with a deep understanding of each pupil as an individual.
Today, the Wetherby family offers two distinct educational pathways, giving families greater choice while maintaining the continuity, quality, and values that have long defined a Wetherby education.
Families can choose between an all-boys or co-educational journey, with a clear pathway from Pre-Prep and Prep School through to Sixth Form at some of London’s most respected private schools.
A New Era for Our Independent Schools in London
From September 2027, the Wetherby family will offer two distinct educational journeys: an all-boys Wetherby School pathway and a co-educational Wetherby Pembridge pathway.
The Wetherby School All-Boys Journey
An all-boys pathway from ages 4 to 18
The Wetherby Pembridge Co-Educational Journey
A co-educational pathway from ages 2 to 18
The Wetherby School Pathway: All-Boys Education From Notting Hill to Marylebone
The Wetherby School pathway offers a continuous single-sex education, built around the way boys learn, develop, and thrive, with a longstanding legacy of preparing them to achieve at the highest level.
Beginning with an established Pre-Prep education and continuing through Prep, Senior School, and Sixth Form, the pathway brings together individual attention, academic ambition, and opportunities well beyond the classroom.
Wetherby School, Notting Hill (Ages 4–7)
A formative start to school life, providing boys with strong academic foundations and individual encouragement, with leading prep school destinations including Westminster Under, St Paul’s Juniors, and King’s College Junior School Wimbledon.
Wetherby School, Marylebone (Currently Wetherby Senior School; Ages 8–18)
An ambitious Prep and Senior School that challenges boys academically while developing the character, independence, and breadth required for university and beyond. Currently welcoming boys from age 11, the school will expand in September 2027 to welcome boys from Year 4 (8+), creating a continuous education through to Sixth Form.
The Wetherby Pembridge Pathway: Co-Educational Schools from Nursery to Sixth Form
The Wetherby Pembridge pathway brings boys and girls together within a connected educational journey from Nursery through to Sixth Form, with a global outlook that prepares pupils to thrive in a changing world.
Combining the heritage and strengths of Wetherby and Pembridge Hall, the pathway offers a modern, future-focused education that develops academic foundations alongside creativity and adaptability.
Wetherby Pembridge Minors (Ages 2-4)
A warm, stimulating introduction to education where children develop curiosity, confidence, and the foundations for a successful start to school.
Wetherby Pembridge Pre-Prep (Currently Wetherby School, Kensington; Ages 4–7)
An academically ambitious environment where personalised teaching, enriching experiences, and individual attention help every child build strong foundations for future learning.
Wetherby Pembridge Prep (Currently Wetherby Prep School; Ages 4–13)
A broad and ambitious Prep School experience in which pupils develop academically, personally, and socially, building the confidence and independence to take on greater challenges.
Wetherby Pembridge (Ages 11–18)
A forward-looking Senior School where pupils are challenged academically, encouraged to pursue their interests, and prepared for university and life beyond school.
Frequently Asked Questions
What are the two Wetherby pathways?
Families can choose between the Wetherby School pathway, which offers an all-boys, single-sex education from ages 4 to 18, and the Wetherby Pembridge pathway, which offers a co-educational journey from ages 2 to 18.
Both provide a connected education from a child’s first school experience through to Sixth Form.
When will the next phase of co-education begin?
The next phase begins in September 2027. Wetherby School Kensington will become Wetherby Pembridge Pre-Prep and begin welcoming girls, while Wetherby Prep School will begin its phased transition to co-education as Wetherby Pembridge Prep.
Applications are already open for girls joining Reception at Wetherby Pembridge Pre-Prep and for Reception and Year 3 at Wetherby Pembridge Prep in September 2027.
What Is Wetherby School Kensington Becoming?
From September 2027, Wetherby School, Kensington, will become Wetherby Pembridge Pre-Prep, welcoming boys and girls aged 4 to 7.
The school will retain its academic ambition, personalised teaching, and individual attention as it begins a new chapter as a co-educational Pre-Prep School in London.
What Is Wetherby Prep School Becoming?
From September 2027, Wetherby Prep School will begin its phased transition to co-education as Wetherby Pembridge Prep.
Girls will initially join Reception and Year 3, with co-education extending through the school over time to establish a co-ed Prep School in London for pupils aged 4 to 13.
What Is Happening to Wetherby Senior School?
Wetherby Senior School will become Wetherby School, Marylebone, extending the all-boys journey to offer a connected education from ages 8 to 18.
Together with Wetherby School, Notting Hill, it will form the Wetherby School pathway from Pre-Prep through to Sixth Form.
Will an All-Boys Wetherby Education Still Be Available?
Yes. Families who prefer a top single-sex education will continue to have an all-boys pathway through Wetherby School, Notting Hill, and Wetherby School, Marylebone.
Maintaining that choice remains an important part of the Wetherby offering.
Which Schools Are Part of the Wetherby School Pathway?
The all-boys journey begins at Wetherby School, Notting Hill and continues at Wetherby School, Marylebone, creating a boys’ school pathway in London from Pre-Prep through to Sixth Form.
Which Schools Are Part of the Wetherby Pembridge Pathway?
The co-educational journey brings together Wetherby Pembridge Minors, Wetherby Pembridge Pre-Prep, Wetherby Pembridge Prep, and Wetherby Pembridge.
Together, these independent schools in London create a connected pathway from Nursery through to Sixth Form, including a top co-ed Pre-Prep School and Prep School.
Will the Schools’ Academic Standards or Ethos Change?
No. The move to co-education builds on the schools' established strengths rather than replacing them. Their academic standards, curricula, pastoral care, and core values will remain in place throughout the transition.
What Are the Benefits of Co-Education?
The benefits of co-education include the opportunity to learn alongside peers with different perspectives, fostering collaboration, adaptability, confidence, and social intelligence.
Learning together also encourages rich discussion, strong problem-solving, and active class participation.
What Are the Benefits of Single-Sex Education?
Single-sex education benefits boys by allowing teaching and pastoral care to be shaped around how they learn, develop, and thrive.
Within the Wetherby School pathway, boys receive individual attention, academic challenge, and opportunities designed to build confidence, independence, and character.
When considering the pros and cons of single-sex education, families can consider their child’s personality, learning preferences, and response to the school environment.
How Do Single-Sex and Co-Ed Schools Differ?
For families comparing a single-sex vs co-ed school, the distinction lies in the learning environment.
Single-sex education can shape teaching and school experiences around boys, while co-education enables pupils to learn alongside boys and girls with varied perspectives. Both Wetherby pathways provide academic ambition, individual attention, pastoral care, and opportunities beyond the classroom.
How Do I Know Which Pathway Is Right for My Child?
Both journeys share the academic ambition, individual attention, and enriching opportunities associated with a Wetherby education.
The choice between a single-sex and co-educational environment will depend on your child’s personality, learning preferences, and needs. Our Admissions teams can help families explore the schools, understand the entry points, and choose a suitable pathway.
Find the Right Independent School in London
Choosing a school is about finding the environment in which your child will thrive. Our Admissions teams can help you explore the all-boys Wetherby School and the co-educational Wetherby Pembridge pathways, understand the opportunities available from Nursery and Pre-Prep through to Sixth Form, and choose a journey suited to your family.

About Us
The Perfect Setting for Every Child to Thrive
The extensive list of inspiring success stories of former students embodies our vision for children to dream big and pursue their unique talents and personal growth.
Wetherby provides an environment that promotes educational excellence and tradition through a forward-thinking, holistic curriculum, which meets the needs of individual pupils. With our individualised learning strategies, each boy learns to challenge himself, pursue high standards, and seek accomplishment in all he does so that his talents shine through.
Our firm commitment is to make sure each boy has a tailored path to help him progress efficiently and leave Wetherby with the practical and intellectual skill set and proactive mindset necessary to thrive in academics and well beyond, having built a solid foundation for success in all future endeavours.
The results speak for themselves: our students achieve the best academic outcomes in London, access the most prestigious prep schools, and later enjoy fascinating careers in various industries.
Our History
In 1951, Margaret and Gerald Russell opened Wetherby School in a smart building on Wetherby Place, Kensington, the basis of what would soon be a highly sought-after independent school.
Today, boys attend three locations – Wetherby Notting Hill, Wetherby Kensington and Wetherby Marylebone – which deliver outstanding pre-prep education. Children aged 4 to 8 learn inside two five-storey Victorian terraced townhouses, easily recognised thanks to the distinctive red doors that are synonymous with Wetherby School. For nearly half a century, generations of young boys have passed through the Wetherby doors wearing the neat grey-and-crimson uniform, the appearance of which has remained largely unchanged for many years.
Wetherby boys flourish in our exceptional, nurturing school environment, carefully crafted to foster their unique talents and unlock their full potential. In the face of striking educational and social change, moreover, Wetherby School has continued to provide the top pre-prep offering in London, while serving as a benchmark of excellence in independent education.
Our Vision
Dream Big, Do Your Best, Be Ready
Wetherby is a vibrant community dedicated to providing the opportunity to pursue dreams, personal excellence and individual growth while celebrating grace, grit and courage.
Pupils are encouraged to develop the skills and proactive mindset to follow their dreams. Contribution and effort is celebrated as much as achievement.
Our curriculum promotes fun, inspires curiosity and ignites a love of learning. We provide personalised learning experiences to cater for the individual needs of pupils.
Pupils are encouraged to express their own views with confidence while learning to respect the opinions and diversity of others. We instil the values of resilience, honesty and kindness to equip them with the self-confidence for future life. We offer a holistic approach to education which fosters positive relationships between home, school and the local community.
Wetherby Through the Years
Wetherby School is founded by Mr and Mrs Gerald Russell in Wetherby Place, London. The school begins educating 100 boys at the Kensington building.
Wetherby moves to Pembridge Square, W2 4ED, and becomes part of Davies, Laing and Dick Educational Group with its own board of governors.
Wetherby School joins the Alpha Plus Group.
Wetherby Preparatory School opens with 24 boys in Year 4. The school grows organically and provides education to 385 boys from Years 3 to 8.
The school moves to larger premises at Bryanston Square and continues to grow.
The school acquires its own sporting facility, Wetherby Sports Ground, in East Acton.
Wetherby Senior School opens in Marylebone.
Alpha Plus acquires premises in Wetherby Gardens, SW5, and opens another school.
Wetherby School Kensington opens in September 2017 as a two-form entry school with classes from Reception to Year 3.
Alpha Plus joins Inspired Education, the global group of premium schools, delivering world-class opportunities for our boys to excel in the classroom and beyond.
Wetherby Marylebone adds a Reception class
Behind the Red Doors
Behind the red doors at Wetherby is a wealth of fun and activity. We believe all boys should be happy, well-rounded and confident learners, who are respectful, thoughtful and motivated Wetherby Ambassadors. Integrity, kindness and good manners are at the heart of what we do.
An atmosphere of care is cultivated inside and outside of school; this is for everyone’s benefit – the children, parents, staff and community – and ensures every boy has a happy, fulfilling school experience. At Wetherby School, we are committed to providing a caring, friendly and safe environment, so that all boys can reach their full potential.
We are very particular about the boys’ manners and conduct both in school and outside. Our boys are proud to wear the Wetherby uniform and be an ambassador for their school. Trust, respect, honesty and a hard-working attitude are intrinsic to everything we teach.
The school year is crammed with activities and learning opportunities, and every single boy will find something in which he will excel. Our motto, “Excellence in Education”, is reflected in everything you will find behind the red doors – academic and pastoral – and promoted by us, the staff, across school life.
Learn more about our school's exemplary learning approach and discover how your child can benefit from over seven decades of academic excellence.

Curriculum
An Ambitious, Integrated Programme to Unleash Our Boys' Full Potential
At our school, we deliver a bespoke academic curriculum, which is dynamic in content and promotes accelerated learning to lead our boys to excellent outcomes. With over seven decades of experience delivering first-rate independent education, we aim to equip pupils with an impressive range of practical and intellectual skills that not only establish a solid foundation for future learning but also prepare them for successful admission to London's top schools.
We believe that an enriching education is most effective when tailored to each child's learning style and pace. As such, our syllabus integrates modern and traditional subject matter and is taught using a child-centred model informed by best practices. Our teachers take the time to understand boys' needs, encourage curiosity, and extend learners' knowledge where possible to help them unlock their full potential.
Curriculum Overview
Our curriculum is broad, balanced, engaging and challenging. Strong reading, writing and numeracy skills are vital, and teachers plan the syllabus carefully to ensure that it establishes these essential competencies while offering continuity in learning and pupil progression. The school's core principle is to cultivate an inspiring setting where all boys work to the very best of their ability. At our school, our pupils strive to succeed and have fun while doing so. In Reception, the aim is to establish a strong foundation for future learning through both structured and child-initiated activities. As children progress through school, teachers increase their efforts to refine their academic skills. We offer as many engaging opportunities for learning and development as possible to thoroughly prepare our boys for their respective 7+ or 8+ entrance examinations.
A Dynamic Programme of Study
The boys follow the school's specially designed dynamic curriculum for mathematics, English, science, integrated curriculum, and Religious Education (R.E.). Reasoning, Learning for Life (Personal, Social, Health and Economic Education), French, music, drama, art, design and technology, computing and physical education (P.E.) are also included in the core curriculum.
The P.E. syllabus offers gymnastics, swimming, football, rugby, cricket and hockey, which, combined with the subjects above, form a holistic, enriching programme of study. Across all year groups, subject specialists teach French, music, drama, art, computing and P.E.
Firm Commitment to Pupil Progress & Development
We take into account the ability of every boy to ensure he is placed on a path that will lead to ongoing achievement in his future education. Boys benefit from the school's personalised approach, which acknowledges and embraces their unique and ever-evolving needs, effectively challenges them and nurtures their talents.
The school's assessment practices are wide-ranging and pupil wellbeing is of great importance to us. We aim to give every child the opportunity to demonstrate their ability in a calm and stress-free environment. The results of periodic assessments allow us to gather comprehensive information on each pupil's progress and act as a point of reference for teachers when designing accelerated learning strategies and necessary interventions.
Establishing Lifelong Skills
During daily learning, the boys work independently and in groups with their classmates, encouraging cooperation while helping them understand the importance of respecting others. Our school places a strong emphasis on pastoral care and the personal development of the boys.
In line with this commitment, we deliver a Learning for Life course, which is an essential aspect of our curriculum as it gives our boys the tools they need to become confident, happy and resilient individuals who are fully capable of attaining continued academic success.
Integrated Curriculum
At our school, pupils are keenly aware of the world around them and their place within it. We aim to nurture their natural curiosity through an innovative Integrated Curriculum, which links different areas of study in a way that emphasises unifying concepts. Our Integrated Curriculum includes traditional subjects, such as history and geography, which are connected through an overarching theme woven into other areas of learning, including art, music and English. By fostering a cross-curricular approach, we empower our boys to apply their knowledge meaningfully to various school subjects and real-life contexts.
In geography and history lessons, our pupils make meaningful connections between various subject areas and transfer their knowledge to real life. Our school's thematic learning approach supports a higher rate of retention of taught material, allowing pupils to contextualise their understanding. Our principal aim is to teach a broad and balanced curriculum that develops each boy’s historical and geographical knowledge, skills and understanding while also emphasising the relevance of the subjects. Lessons seek to engage pupils so that they can appreciate the influence of these subjects on their past, present and future. When designing lessons for the Integrated Curriculum, we are aiming to foster an enjoyment of history and geography from an early age. We deliver the curriculum through a skills-centred approach, extending the boys’ natural curiosity of the world around them and encouraging them to question, explain, problem-solve and describe their knowledge and understanding of each topic in the syllabus. We equip pupils with the ability to make decisions, evaluate evidence based on a range of sources, record information, and communicate their knowledge in a variety of ways. In the first few years of learning, it is of prime importance to introduce early concepts via a diverse and exciting curriculum. To do this in the most effective way possible, our experienced teachers create interactive lessons that enable pupils to investigate, explore and evaluate the topics they are studying. As a result, children develop their ideas in a fun and engaging way. To further solidify teacher-led learning, we provide opportunities for the boys to expand upon the syllabus through educational trips and workshops, a wealth of subject-specific resources (e.g., books), primary and secondary sources and various technologies (e.g., iPads, virtual reality).

English
Literacy is an essential part of our curriculum and forms the basis of our early learning approach. Our boys receive an exceptional British education centred upon an exemplary English-led Literacy curriculum. At Wetherby, we understand the importance of teaching key literacy skills effectively, as its effect on children's lives is unparalleled. Our teachers provide high-quality learning experiences that build a concrete understanding of core literary practices, foster a genuine love of writing and ensure our boys develop a passion for reading a variety of genres at an early age. From Reception to Year 3, English lessons are broken into key subjects designed to develop the crucial skills of speaking, listening, reading and writing. Proficiency in these areas allows pupils to communicate effectively and express themselves creatively and imaginatively.

Literacy Events
Throughout the year, boys are involved in activities such as World Book Day, Poetry Day, a spelling bee, visiting author workshops, national competitions for poetry and short stories, and educational visits.
Maths
Mathematics teaches boys how to make sense of the world around them by developing their ability to calculate, reason and solve problems. Lessons are interactive, and our boys are introduced to the relationships and patterns in numbers and how to apply this knowledge to their day-to-day lives. As their knowledge and understanding grow, pupils learn to appreciate and apply mathematical concepts to a range of different contexts.
The school's mathematics curriculum aims to:
Mathematics lessons are delivered daily across all year groups. Lessons emphasise the four operations and number bonds, and boys are supported to carry out mental calculations and a range of problem-solving techniques. Our maths teachers are passionate about their roles and spend a great deal of time explaining each concept in a practical manner before transferring pupils' understanding to more formal applications.
The Reception curriculum lays the foundation for future understanding by introducing various key concepts. In Year 1, subject material becomes more advanced, and boys become better acquainted with the formalities of a more traditional maths syllabus while employing practical learning opportunities in each term. As boys progress through the school, teaching emphasises the more formal aspects of mathematics, which are a requirement for entrance examinations.
Reasoning
Reasoning skills are viewed by many in the educational field as a meaningful indicator of innate intelligence, and assessment in this area is given significant importance in academic testing processes from 7+ level onwards. Our school is unique in its delivery of reasoning education: our exceptional curriculum cultivates the skills needed to effectively solve problems while encouraging boys to apply their newfound skills to contexts that they are familiar with, allowing their talents to shine through.
While some academics would argue that it is ‘impossible to teach reasoning skills,’ at Wetherby, learners benefit from and enjoy being exposed to a range of non-verbal and verbal reasoning activities. We introduce concepts as early as possible to allow boys to gain familiarity with the process of tackling tasks. Our pupils achieve impressive rates of success in entrance examinations, which is a testament to the efficacy of our teaching approach. We believe that, when guided effectively, children can learn strategies to complete tasks while developing their capacity to think logically.
Reasoning Curriculum Content
Our curriculum places equal emphasis on non-verbal and verbal reasoning skills. The non-verbal aspect of the curriculum fosters the ability to identify patterns and sequences, and understand and analyse visual information. At our school, we aim to go beyond the teaching of simple fluency or vocabulary recognition. We deliver verbal reasoning lessons that develop boys’ capacity to understand and assimilate verbal information and think constructively about language.
Our pupil-centred approach allows boys to learn at their own pace and increase their knowledge according to their current ability level. This in turn builds their self-confidence and nurtures their talents in public speaking and communication.
Lessons are enhanced by a wide range of practical resources and formal materials to further reinforce instruction. Boys are assessed in reasoning through standardised NFER testing methods from the end of their Reception year onwards. Our small class sizes allow teachers to pay close attention to each boy’s ongoing performance during classwork and closely monitor his progress, enabling them to support or challenge him appropriately.
Science
Science has an immeasurable impact on our lives and is fascinating to explore. Our pupils are taught to appreciate the far-reaching applications of science and learn how scientific concepts can be utilised to explain the changes they observe in the world around them. Pupils are encouraged to use reasoning skills to hypothesise and predict possible outcomes. They participate in practical experiments to observe effects and analyse causes. We deliver the science curriculum in engaging, inspiring lessons and workshops that cover the essential aspects of scientific concepts, including processes and applications.
We aim to enable children to be bold in their scientific questioning by inspiring curiosity and supporting each pupil to have the confidence to ask 'why' and 'how'. By delivering a diverse and interactive science curriculum, pupils deepen their understanding of each topic by developing their investigative and problem-solving skills through a systematic, methodical and creative approach. Over time, our boys begin to appreciate the impact that science will have in the future on a personal, national and global level, and we encourage boys to recognise the power they have to influence the world around them positively.
Enrichment workshops complement lessons and give the boys a platform to develop their knowledge, discuss pertinent topics and continue building a passion for the subject. From the Reception stage to Year 3, the science curriculum comprises up-to-date material and focuses on practical and investigative work. By introducing children to a body of core, foundational concepts, we ensure pupils are able to recognise the power of rational explanation and develop a sense of excitement and curiosity regarding natural phenomena.
Practical experiments are organised regularly, giving boys the opportunity to participate in immersive lessons that demonstrate theoretical concepts and allow boys to apply their reasoning skills. During fun, hands-on individual and group practical activities, boys are encouraged to form theories, observe processes and record changes independently and as a group. Science allows our pupils to explain the unknown in ways they never imagined. Our school is delighted to support our pupils' journey towards understanding by harnessing the mystery of the unknown and channelling it into effective educational experiences children can enjoy.

Scholarships & Bursaries
Building a Diverse, Exceptional School Community
Our school offers scholarships to exceptional applicants who wish to join either Wetherby School Notting Hill or Kensington, along with bursaries for current students.
As a school, we are proud to provide best-in-class learning experiences that enable our boys to become happy, confident, multi-skilled individuals. Scholarships allow Wetherby School to expand its community by welcoming students from different backgrounds, including boys who are highly gifted yet lack the resources to access a transformative education. This has the added benefit of fostering diverse classrooms that are inclusive and enriching for all. The provision of bursaries aims to assist families of current students who have fallen unexpectedly into personal/financial difficulty.
Nsouli Scholars: A Transformative Opportunity
The Nsouli Scholars Programme is an exciting global initiative that promises to transform lives by enabling 50 extraordinary students at any one time to attend any of Inspired’s prestigious schools on a full scholarship for the duration of their education. The ambition is that the scholarship will provide hundreds of children with an opportunity to receive a truly transformative education.
By opening this path to exceptional individuals, we hope to expand our community, and to empower children of all backgrounds with unrivalled opportunities in academics, sports, the arts and extracurricular activities. In this sense, the Nsouli Scholars Programme is an investment both in education and in shaping the leaders of tomorrow.
This generous endowment honours Nadim Nsouli, who founded Inspired in 2013 as a definitive statement of excellence in private international education. In recognition of Mr Nsouli’s Lebanese heritage and Inspired’s commitment to inclusivity, several scholarships will be awarded to individuals of Lebanese origin.
Gold Standard Charitable Trust
We warmly invite families to apply for a scholarship or bursary for their child to attend Wetherby School Notting Hill or Kensington.
Financial support for our pupils is administered by the Gold Standard Charitable Trust (GSCT), which raises funds for all Inspired UK Schools. After receiving the short-listed candidates from the Head of the School, GSCT does a means test to confirm eligibility and make a decision. Successful applicants will receive between 50% and 110% of the cost of tuition.
Inspired schools offer a world-class educational experience that combines academics and engaging extra-curricular activities, producing confident, multi-skilled students who flourish in a competitive and increasingly interconnected world. Along with expert instruction by hand-picked teachers, our students access specialist sports programmes and professional tutelage from leaders in the performing and creative arts. As a result, they leave armed with a robust value system and a love of learning that extends well beyond the classroom.
Inspired is also committed to leveraging new and transformative learning technologies. Inspired AI empowers children to achieve academic excellence by delivering actionable insights that are unique to each student, including strengths and weaknesses. Our partnership with The Royal College of Music and Forte, a revolutionary online platform, enables children to receive personalised music tuition from professionals. Wetherby School: Two Pathways, One Exceptional Education in London
For more than 75 years, Wetherby has been synonymous with exceptional independent education in London, combining academic ambition with a deep understanding of each pupil as an individual.
Today, the Wetherby family offers two distinct educational pathways, giving families greater choice while maintaining the continuity, quality, and values that have long defined a Wetherby education.
Families can choose between an all-boys or co-educational journey, with a clear pathway from Pre-Prep and Prep School through to Sixth Form at some of London’s most respected private schools.
A New Era for Our Independent Schools in London
From September 2027, the Wetherby family will offer two distinct educational journeys: an all-boys Wetherby School pathway and a co-educational Wetherby Pembridge pathway.
The Wetherby School All-Boys Journey
An all-boys pathway from ages 4 to 18
The Wetherby Pembridge Co-Educational Journey
A co-educational pathway from ages 2 to 18
The Wetherby School Pathway: All-Boys Education From Notting Hill to Marylebone
The Wetherby School pathway offers a continuous single-sex education, built around the way boys learn, develop, and thrive, with a longstanding legacy of preparing them to achieve at the highest level.
Beginning with an established Pre-Prep education and continuing through Prep, Senior School, and Sixth Form, the pathway brings together individual attention, academic ambition, and opportunities well beyond the classroom.
Wetherby School, Notting Hill (Ages 4–7)
A formative start to school life, providing boys with strong academic foundations and individual encouragement, with leading prep school destinations including Westminster Under, St Paul’s Juniors, and King’s College Junior School Wimbledon.
Wetherby School, Marylebone (Currently Wetherby Senior School; Ages 8–18)
An ambitious Prep and Senior School that challenges boys academically while developing the character, independence, and breadth required for university and beyond. Currently welcoming boys from age 11, the school will expand in September 2027 to welcome boys from Year 4 (8+), creating a continuous education through to Sixth Form.
The Wetherby Pembridge Pathway: Co-Educational Schools from Nursery to Sixth Form
The Wetherby Pembridge pathway brings boys and girls together within a connected educational journey from Nursery through to Sixth Form, with a global outlook that prepares pupils to thrive in a changing world.
Combining the heritage and strengths of Wetherby and Pembridge Hall, the pathway offers a modern, future-focused education that develops academic foundations alongside creativity and adaptability.
Wetherby Pembridge Minors (Ages 2-4)
A warm, stimulating introduction to education where children develop curiosity, confidence, and the foundations for a successful start to school.
Wetherby Pembridge Pre-Prep (Currently Wetherby School, Kensington; Ages 4–7)
An academically ambitious environment where personalised teaching, enriching experiences, and individual attention help every child build strong foundations for future learning.
Wetherby Pembridge Prep (Currently Wetherby Prep School; Ages 4–13)
A broad and ambitious Prep School experience in which pupils develop academically, personally, and socially, building the confidence and independence to take on greater challenges.
Wetherby Pembridge (Ages 11–18)
A forward-looking Senior School where pupils are challenged academically, encouraged to pursue their interests, and prepared for university and life beyond school.
Frequently Asked Questions
What are the two Wetherby pathways?
Families can choose between the Wetherby School pathway, which offers an all-boys, single-sex education from ages 4 to 18, and the Wetherby Pembridge pathway, which offers a co-educational journey from ages 2 to 18.
Both provide a connected education from a child’s first school experience through to Sixth Form.
When will the next phase of co-education begin?
The next phase begins in September 2027. Wetherby School Kensington will become Wetherby Pembridge Pre-Prep and begin welcoming girls, while Wetherby Prep School will begin its phased transition to co-education as Wetherby Pembridge Prep.
Applications are already open for girls joining Reception at Wetherby Pembridge Pre-Prep and for Reception and Year 3 at Wetherby Pembridge Prep in September 2027.
What Is Wetherby School Kensington Becoming?
From September 2027, Wetherby School, Kensington, will become Wetherby Pembridge Pre-Prep, welcoming boys and girls aged 4 to 7.
The school will retain its academic ambition, personalised teaching, and individual attention as it begins a new chapter as a co-educational Pre-Prep School in London.
What Is Wetherby Prep School Becoming?
From September 2027, Wetherby Prep School will begin its phased transition to co-education as Wetherby Pembridge Prep.
Girls will initially join Reception and Year 3, with co-education extending through the school over time to establish a co-ed Prep School in London for pupils aged 4 to 13.
What Is Happening to Wetherby Senior School?
Wetherby Senior School will become Wetherby School, Marylebone, extending the all-boys journey to offer a connected education from ages 8 to 18.
Together with Wetherby School, Notting Hill, it will form the Wetherby School pathway from Pre-Prep through to Sixth Form.
Will an All-Boys Wetherby Education Still Be Available?
Yes. Families who prefer a top single-sex education will continue to have an all-boys pathway through Wetherby School, Notting Hill, and Wetherby School, Marylebone.
Maintaining that choice remains an important part of the Wetherby offering.
Which Schools Are Part of the Wetherby School Pathway?
The all-boys journey begins at Wetherby School, Notting Hill and continues at Wetherby School, Marylebone, creating a boys’ school pathway in London from Pre-Prep through to Sixth Form.
Which Schools Are Part of the Wetherby Pembridge Pathway?
The co-educational journey brings together Wetherby Pembridge Minors, Wetherby Pembridge Pre-Prep, Wetherby Pembridge Prep, and Wetherby Pembridge.
Together, these independent schools in London create a connected pathway from Nursery through to Sixth Form, including a top co-ed Pre-Prep School and Prep School.
Will the Schools’ Academic Standards or Ethos Change?
No. The move to co-education builds on the schools' established strengths rather than replacing them. Their academic standards, curricula, pastoral care, and core values will remain in place throughout the transition.
What Are the Benefits of Co-Education?
The benefits of co-education include the opportunity to learn alongside peers with different perspectives, fostering collaboration, adaptability, confidence, and social intelligence.
Learning together also encourages rich discussion, strong problem-solving, and active class participation.
What Are the Benefits of Single-Sex Education?
Single-sex education benefits boys by allowing teaching and pastoral care to be shaped around how they learn, develop, and thrive.
Within the Wetherby School pathway, boys receive individual attention, academic challenge, and opportunities designed to build confidence, independence, and character.
When considering the pros and cons of single-sex education, families can consider their child’s personality, learning preferences, and response to the school environment.
How Do Single-Sex and Co-Ed Schools Differ?
For families comparing a single-sex vs co-ed school, the distinction lies in the learning environment.
Single-sex education can shape teaching and school experiences around boys, while co-education enables pupils to learn alongside boys and girls with varied perspectives. Both Wetherby pathways provide academic ambition, individual attention, pastoral care, and opportunities beyond the classroom.
How Do I Know Which Pathway Is Right for My Child?
Both journeys share the academic ambition, individual attention, and enriching opportunities associated with a Wetherby education.
The choice between a single-sex and co-educational environment will depend on your child’s personality, learning preferences, and needs. Our Admissions teams can help families explore the schools, understand the entry points, and choose a suitable pathway.
Find the Right Independent School in London
Choosing a school is about finding the environment in which your child will thrive. Our Admissions teams can help you explore the all-boys Wetherby School and the co-educational Wetherby Pembridge pathways, understand the opportunities available from Nursery and Pre-Prep through to Sixth Form, and choose a journey suited to your family.

75 Years of Wetherby and Pembridge Hall Excellence

Originally named Our Lady of Sion, it moved to 18 Pembridge Square in 1980 and became Pembridge Hall. From these modest beginnings, it grew into one of West London’s most prominent independent preparatory schools for girls, later expanding to a second building at 10 Pembridge Square.
Over the decades, Pembridge Hall has established its own proud tradition of academic preparation and personal development. As a leader in girls’ education, it nurtures pupils’ confidence, independence, and individual talents, preparing them to flourish at leading senior schools.

In our fully resourced art room, pupils discover and refine their creative skills, while generous outdoor areas allow for much-needed physical exercise and play. Our dedicated school hall hosts weekly assemblies and fosters a sense of identity and belonging to the Wetherby School Notting Hill community. A cosy, state-of-the-art library with extensive materials allows pupils to extend their learning and explore and study in a quiet setting.
Premium Off-Site Facilities
Our prestigious partnerships with local organisations provide boys with unique opportunities to refine their artistic and sporting abilities in first-class off-site facilities.
With drama productions at the Tabernacle theatre, Wetherby School Notting Hill boys gain valuable experience by performing in a well-established, professional space that has hosted acclaimed singers James Blunt and Sam Lee, among others.
Our pupils develop their physical and sporting skills in safe, fully-equipped local leisure centres with courts and pools perfect for swimmers of all ability levels, and the extensive pitches at Inspired Sports Grounds. Pembridge Square, Perks Field and Kensington Gardens Square offer additional quiet and expansive areas for supervised outdoor activities.
Discover how our private pre-prep school in Notting Hill can unlock your boy's full potential with a meticulously planned early education programme, and prepare him for a lifetime of success and accomplishment.

An Inspired School
Inspiring Excellence with an Ambitious, All-Rounded Education
Wetherby School is part of Inspired Education, a leading global group of premium private schools with 95,000+ students across 6 continents. As an Inspired School, we are committed to developing our boys’ full potential by helping them achieve excellent academic results and delivering various exciting learning experiences. Cutting-edge teaching and learning provision, superb facilities and access to a global community are merely a handful of the guaranteed benefits that come with being part of Inspired Education. Our young learners harness these regularly and, in doing so, become confident, independent, multi-skilled individuals.
Learn More About Inspired
The Three Pillars of an Inspired School Education
Exceptional outcomes are integral to Inspired’s philosophy, which extends beyond the confines of traditional academia. From Reception to Year 3, we support boys with a holistic, innovative school experience premised on the three Pillars of an Inspired Education: Academics, Sport, and Performing & Creative Arts. By fostering excellence in these key areas, Wetherby seeks to deliver an integrated educational offering that is challenging and empowering for learners, and secures their success in the long term.
High-quality academic provision is central to an education at all Inspired schools. Through active engagement in the learning process, children are taught to think critically and gain increased confidence in their own abilities and a thirst for knowledge. Achievement in academics provides learners with a path to future opportunities in work and university; for this reason, Inspired hand-picks teachers who are highly experienced and committed to unlocking learners’ full potential.
Performing and Creative Arts
Performing and Creative Arts
According to research, encouraging creativity in children leads to improved learning engagement and overall well-being. Opportunities for artistic expression allow students to cultivate crucial life skills in addition to enjoying an all-rounded education. From problem-solving to divergent thinking, Inspired learners gain a variety of competencies and are pushed to explore new and existing interests, including drama, music, visual arts and more. In doing so, they learn to display confidence while also gaining lifelong passions and proficiencies.
As an Inspired school, we are committed to delivering excellent sports opportunities. Sports are a crucial opportunity for our boys to develop strong personal qualities, such as discipline and teamwork, and foster their physical and mental well-being. In addition to Physical Education (P.E.), boys enjoy access to a range of after-school activities, including cricket, football and martial arts.
Inspired Schools Around the World
Inspired Education Head Office Address: 6th Floor, 3 Burlington Gardens, London W1S 3EP Inspired Education Head Office Phone Number: 020 3867 9961

House System
Encouraging Excellence and Camaraderie
Our school is not just a place of exceptional learning and teaching, but a supportive, dynamic and creative environment in which our boys are empowered and inspired to explore the full extent of their abilities. The House System is an integral part of our school and gives each boy a sense of belonging on a personal level. It is also used to reward learners for their conduct and achievements across many aspects of school life, encouraging and reinforcing their commitment to positive outcomes.
All boys are assigned a house before they enrol at Wetherby School, including those that arrive midway through the academic year. They remain in their house for the duration of their enrolment.
Notting Hill and Kensington have separate House Systems in place, with four School Houses per site. At the beginning of the year, House Captains are elected by students and staff to provide a good example for their peers during daily activities and help lead school-wide events, such as the annual Sports Day.
Collective House Rewards
Celebrating Our Boys' Achievement
Boys receive House points for being a Wetherby Ambassador, academic achievement and demonstrating effort in their learning. They are given a counter to put in their House Collection Box and points are recorded on charts displayed in the boys’ classrooms.
Children attend year group assemblies, during which stickers and certificates are awarded to the House that has received the most points. The total number of points earned is presented on the House Points Display Board. Each week, a picture of the House Cup is placed next to the triumphant Houses.
The House that receives the most points by the end of the term will win the House Cup. Whole-school assemblies are an excellent opportunity for all students to gather together in celebration of their achievements and efforts. In addition to the autumn and spring end-of-term assemblies, the cup is also presented to the winning House at the summer prize-giving ceremony.
School Houses at Notting Hill
At Notting Hill, Houses are named after famous British military leaders. Each House has an associated colour, which is detailed below.

Learning Support
Fostering Excellence Across All Ability Levels
Our school is non-selective and welcomes children of all ability levels. We aim to give our boys the best start in their educational journey by understanding the needs of each child before they enrol. Throughout your child's time at our school, staff members work closely with boys to monitor their progress and provide additional support where necessary. The school selects staff who have unrivalled experience delivering tailored learning strategies. Together with our highly motivated teaching assistants, our teachers support a thriving community of boys, each of whom possesses unique skills and talents. Some boys may require additional support in specific areas; as such, we have a large and committed in-house learning support team who are more than happy to offer their assistance and guidance to both pupils and their parents.
Learning Support Team
The Head of Learning Support works closely with class teachers, as well as a range of other educational professionals, including dyslexia specialists, and speech and language therapists. Additionally, the school maintains strong links with external agencies and regularly consults with educational psychologists, occupational therapists, behavioural optometrists, dyslexic centres and play therapists to provide 360-degree support.
At Wetherby School, we understand that each boy learns in his own unique way. As experienced educators, our teachers recognise that differentiation in class is essential to ensure all learners achieve all they are capable of at each stage of their academic journey; therefore, when needed, they provide tailored exercises and adapted activities. All staff members receive ongoing SEND (special educational needs and disability) training and are actively involved in the identification of additional needs, pupil target setting and the assessment process. Across year groups, teachers periodically review boys' individual targets to monitor their progress and keep them on track.
Tailored Learning Strategies
We believe early identification and intervention is the key to future success and have different levels of support which we can offer boys who require extra help. Our boys receive high-quality first teaching with additional learning strategies, access to early morning booster groups, small group interventions and one-to-one specialist teaching assistance.
Wetherby is proud of the learning support it provides. We treat each child as an individual and tailor the support they receive to suit their specific needs. Underpinning all our work is the desire to build a child’s confidence in believing they can achieve and succeed at school and beyond.
Learn more about how our school's comprehensive learning support services can introduce your child to limitless opportunities for success.

Student Enrichment
Inspiring Strategies to Unlock Our Boys' Full Potential
Providing a holistic education is critical if we are to elicit the very best from our learners. By enjoying a breadth of activities in class and out, our boys have the opportunity to gain key competencies – from teamwork and leadership skills to confidence, critical reasoning and emotional literacy – and develop into happy, considerate, well-rounded individuals.
Our school offers a range of stimulating extracurriculars to inspire boys and foster development in different areas, including sports, the arts and academia. Children of all ability levels are supported and encouraged to reach their full potential: by delivering a wealth of rich opportunities, we help our students to explore new interests, develop existing ones, and empower them with varied, valuable skills for later life.
At Wetherby School, we aim to instil core values in our boys from an early age, furthering their growth into caring, respectful and responsible individuals. Our curriculum promotes fundamental British values, good behaviours and attitudes, and other attributes that enable our boys to excel in both school and the wider world. We encourage boys to engage positively with the school community; by doing so, and by taking on additional responsibilities, they emerge capable, independent and with a strong sense of accountability.
Our school is a welcoming community dedicated to giving boys valuable opportunities to demonstrate their skills and thrive as well-rounded young learners who actively seek to improve their learning environment. The School Council ensures boys are able to contribute towards the continuous improvement of teaching and learning. By meeting with senior leadership and discussing pertinent issues, elected student representatives create a more harmonious and positive community for all. Aims
The School Council aims to: • Make a positive contribution to the school environment and ethos; • Develop and promote boys’ self-confidence, social skills and their responsibilities towards each other, teachers and adult members of staff; • Develop the boys’ knowledge, skills and understanding of how to contribute to society as a whole and what it means to be an active citizen; • Develop boys’ speaking and listening skills; • Allow the boys to have a voice and to share their ideas and opinions with others; • Develop the boys’ recognition of themselves as worthwhile individuals with a right to be heard; • Allow the boys to become more responsible and actively involved in the decision-making process of the school; • Develop important life skills that promote positive mental health and social welfare, emotional literacy, critical and moral reasoning, self-esteem, self-awareness, communication skills, relationship skills and assertiveness; and • Increase self-esteem and self-confidence.
Wetherby School Kensington Pupil Parliament
Our Vision
A school is a community. Our Pupil Parliament helps to make Wetherby School Kensington a more harmonious, inclusive, and empowering place to learn. It is a platform through which pupils actively contribute to school improvement and take part in shaping the school’s future.
Aims
• To make a positive contribution to the school environment and ethos. • To develop and promote pupils’ self-confidence, social skills, and sense of responsibility. • To empower pupils to understand how they can positively contribute to society and become active citizens. • To develop pupils’ speaking, listening, and critical thinking skills. • To ensure all pupils have a meaningful voice in school life and to share their ideas and opinions with others. • To foster recognition of every child as a valued individual with the right to be heard. • To encourage responsibility, collaboration, and participation in decision-making. • To promote life skills that support emotional literacy, mental health, and social well being. • To increase self-esteem and personal motivation through purposeful leadership roles.
The Wetherby Ambassador Rules are the foundation of the school's behaviour management policy. These rules outline the conduct that is expected from each learner in addition to forming the basis of our weekly whole-school targets. At the beginning of the school year, boys are reminded of these rules, and they are referred to across all year levels, especially during Learning for Life lessons. When a rule has been broken, teachers use the opportunity to discuss the importance of good behaviour.
The Wetherby Ambassador Rules are:
Each week in assembly, one boy from each year group is given an award for being an exemplary Wetherby Ambassador. His photograph is also taken and displayed on the Wetherby Ambassador noticeboard to commemorate his achievements.
We are polite, kind and helpful;
We work hard and try our best;
We smile and have fun;
We always tell the truth;
We learn from our mistakes;
We listen to and respect others;
We have a growth mindset; and
Co-curricular Activities
We are delighted to deliver a wide variety of engaging and creative activities that enrich the lives of boys beyond the classroom. Our co-curricular provision is comprehensive and includes both lunchtime and after-school clubs. Boys may choose to participate in additional academic courses, receive sports coaching or gain art and music tuition. All activities offer an exciting opportunity for our curious learners to have fun, make new friends and explore their talents in a range of contexts.
After-School Clubs
During term time, we run an extensive after-school activities programme that includes the following clubs:
There are four choirs at Wetherby School, and boys may join in Years 1, 2 or 3, subject to a successful audition. The choir is led by the Head of Music and rehearsals are held weekly for each year group in the music room or hall.

Trips
Trips are a vital part of a boy’s pre-prep education. They complement in-class learning and enhance pupils' understanding of the school curriculum. Each year, staff organise numerous outings for all year groups, ensuring children benefit from the wealth of cultural and historical places of interest located conveniently close to our school. Parents will receive details of school trips well beforehand.
In Year 3, all boys take part in a residential trip for three days and two nights.
After spending time with their friends immersed in nature, our boys gain an increased sense of independence, crucial life skills, confidence in their teamwork and leadership abilities, and many amazing stories! At the Parent Information Evening in the autumn term of Year 3, parents and guardians will receive further details regarding the residential trip.
Nurturing Exceptional Abilities
We encourage each boy to excel across the curriculum as a whole. Class and specialist teachers are responsible for identifying children with exceptional ability in a particular subject/s or area. We aim to identify able children as early as possible so that we can monitor and support their progress effectively.
Personal Traits
• Inquisitive, curious, alert and responsive to new ideas • Quick or agile thinker • High self-motivation/initiative; can work well independently • Socially adept • Leadership qualities • Good/unusual sense of humour • Sensitive nature, or sensitivity and empathy with others • Socially immature or isolated; may prefer computers to people
Learning Ability
• Learns new ideas and concepts quickly, easily and readily • Good at reasoning and demonstrates logical or analytical thinking skills • Good at dealing with abstractions or abstract thinking • Ability to identify relationships between things; can generalise from specific facts • Good at understanding concepts; offers unusual insights • Ability to memorise information quickly and easily • Follows complex directions easily • Keen powers of observation • Has advanced vocabulary, is verbally fluent and is self-expressive • Early reading ability, often before school age and demonstrates rapid reading • Good attention span and can concentrate; can persevere for long periods if interested
• Dislikes closed tasks and learning concepts repetitively; may get bored easily • Informed of, or may show interest in, ideas and concepts beyond their years • Creative and imaginative; demonstrates original problem-solving ideas; artistic or musical talent • Inclined to choose unusual but effective methods of working, perhaps by using a different line of logic or by jumping steps • Many interests or hobbies; reads across a wide range of subjects • May prefer verbal expression • May resent imposed timetable restrictions if interested in a task • Perfectionists
Our Learning for Life (PSHEE) Programme
The Learning for Life programme is part of the Personal, Social, Health and Economic Education (PSHEE) curriculum. This programme, taught from Reception to Year 3, aims to reinforce good attitudes and behaviours and develop key skills and attributes such as self-esteem, risk management, resilience, teamwork and critical thinking. It does so in the context of learning grouped into four core themes: health and wellbeing, relationships, digital safety and living in the wider world (including economic wellbeing and aspects of career education). In addition, PSHEE lessons seek to help boys understand attributes essential to overall happiness, such as cooperation and respect for property, the environment and, above all, each other.
Learn more about the rewarding opportunities we can offer your son to nurture his potential and lead him towards success in the classroom and beyond.
Roles & Responsibilities
There are many daily responsibilities that boys may carry out in their classrooms. Roles include snack monitor and cloakroom monitor. There are also several roles and responsibilities that boys can take on outside of the classroom, giving them the chance to develop confidence, leadership skills and teamwork abilities. Boys who choose to take on additional responsibility are given a badge to show the title of their role.
Student roles include: • Charity Ambassador • Eco-Warrior • School Council Representative • Library Monitor
